newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures ricochet to lower close.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures ricochet to lower close.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ricocheted around during erratic afternoon trading, finally plopping back down to end moderately lower.
Traders tied the final leg lower to erosion in U.S. Treasury bond futures and to signs of options-related positioning ahead of Friday's expiration of January options.
Some also said the market's thin, spotty turnover exacerbated price swings, with locals seen dominating trade that featured mainly 10- and 20-lots as big players refrained.
"It's all goofy," said one Standard & Poor's 500 futures broker of the afternoon's gyrations.

"We watched the volatility in bonds...and the NASDAQ's down 19.85 points," added the floor broker. "The Dow made a huge rally and got all the way back up to almost even and then they started selling off again."
He noted periodic spurts of buying and selling throughout the afternoon, although traders said they saw little evidence of arbitrage programs during most of the session.

"There weren't really buy programs at all," the broker added, saying March S&P 500s during the quick afternoon sprint upward to the day's peak mainly stayed shy of premium levels seen as wide enough to attract arbitrage buy programs.
Fair value Wednesday based on LIBOR was roughly 4.75 points over cash. Arb buy programs needed about 5.65 points premium and sells needed roughly 3.85 points over.

Technically, March S&P 500s briefly broke below support seen near the 768.60 level but recovered handily and filled in a so-called "liquidity" gap near 774.85. The contract stalled, however, after probing above a near-term objective one chartist pegged at 776.00.
"I want to know what took this (rally) so long," the chartist said of the afternoon's pop up to the day's high. "It's a bull market."

Others said they would reserve judgment on the durability of the contract's recent rally until after the serial options expiry is completed and the market settles in from its gyrations sparked by Intel Corp's quarterly earnings.
Intel late Tuesday said it earned $2.13 a share vs $0.98. That compared to the First Call consensus forecast of $1.84.

March S&P 500s settled down 1.55 at 771.65, Value Lines lost 1.25 to 700.35, Nikkei rose 265.0 to 18,225.0, Midcap eased 0.55 to 264.20, NYSE Composite eased 0.15 to 407.10, Russell dropped 2.10 to 369.75, and NASDAQ 100 futures skidded 19.85 points to 871.15.
